svg.title: Batch noise falls with the batch size and is zero at 300
svg.desc: A chart on logarithmic axes of the root-mean-square distance between a batch gradient and the full-batch gradient against the batch size B from 1 to 300, on the spiral network at fixed weights in float64. Diamonds: measured over 2,000 random batches per size, 3.0115 at 1, 1.0647 at 8, 0.5124 at 32, 0.2489 at 100, 0.2069 at 128, 0.0000 at 300; the value 0 at 300 is marked on the bottom edge. A solid line: the closed form sigma over root B times the root of (N minus B) over (N minus 1), with sigma 3.0631 and N = 300, which bends down to 0 at B = 300. A dashed line: sigma over root B alone, a straight line on these axes, 0.1768 at 300. A dotted line marks the length of the full gradient, 0.4570. A table at the right lists the measured value and both closed forms for each size.
svg.text: Batch noise falls with the batch size and is zero at 300
The spiral network at fixed weights, float64, N = 300: a batch gradient's distance from the full one.
closed form, rows drawn without replacement
At B = 32 the noise is still 1.12 times the length of the gradient it estimates.
